text:
Recent work supports text as a useful signal, but does not establish gains for this exact scratch-trained BERT4Rec configuration. [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates attribute-aware text representations and matching, but uses pretrained language models. [AlterRec (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.ijcnlp-long.12.pdf) identifies a relevant failure mode: naive ID/text fusion can underperform ID-only models because ID features dominate optimization and text remains undertrained. Its separate optimization approach is not directly applicable under the required jointly trained single-model constraint.

A plausible experiment—not a verified literature result—is a small randomly initialized word-embedding encoder with pooling or a CNN over titles/descriptions, projected into item-embedding space and jointly trained inside one BERT4Rec. Normalize ID and text features before a learned residual fusion; monitor text-encoder gradients and validate against the corrected ID-only baseline. This preserves one network and one checkpoint per category, without pretrained weights or separately fitted scores.

Leakage prevention is essential: [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) uses masked-item reconstruction because bidirectional inputs otherwise expose prediction targets. For the proposed extension, replace both the selected item ID and its associated text features at masked positions; masking only the ID leaves a semantic shortcut. Candidate-side title/description encoding remains legitimate for scoring, provided target content never enters the history representation through the masked position. Use appended-mask inference and read its final nonpadding position. No retrieved study establishes an improvement under the specified four-category RecHarness protocol.
